sections.title: One URL. Multiple clips.

sections.title: Built to post more, not edit more

Built for streamers, podcasts, YouTubers, and small studios that need several clips per week.

sections.title: Simple credits, no surprises
body: You spend credits based on source duration. A free account lets you try. Creator and Studio plans unlock more volume.
No card required to start.

docs.title: Upcut docs
docs.lead: Everything you need to generate your first batch of clips in a few minutes.

sections.title: 1. Create an account
body: Sign up on Upcut (email or Google). The free tier includes source minutes so you can test the pipeline without a card.

sections.title: 2. Paste a URL
body: From the dashboard, paste a YouTube link or Twitch VOD. Upcut estimates duration and credit cost before you start.

sections.title: 3. Choose your options
body: Target clip duration, 9:16 or 1:1 format, subtitle style, auto or manual mode (search window on the timeline).
Confirm: the job enters the queue. Track progress in the project.

sections.title: 4. Download and post
body: When rendering is done, preview each clip, tweak if needed, then download the MP4.
Post to TikTok, YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, or Snapchat — the file is already the right ratio.

sections.title: Tips
body: Clear speech sources = better subtitles and better moments.
For long VODs, manual mode (zone + duration) avoids burning credits on the whole video.
See the blog for short-form guides, and /product for product detail.

transformer-youtube-en-shorts.title: Turn a YouTube video into Shorts
transformer-youtube-en-shorts.lead: You already have the content. What’s missing is short-form volume. Here’s a clear process from long video to postable clips.

sections.title: What actually works in short-form
body: Shorts that retain start strong (first 3 seconds), carry one clear idea, and stay readable without sound thanks to subtitles.
Don’t republish 10 minutes vertically: aim for 15–60 seconds, one punchline, one demo, one reaction.

sections.title: Manual method (no tool)
body: 1) Note 3–5 timestamps where energy spikes. 2) Export those cuts. 3) Reframe to 9:16. 4) Add subtitles. 5) Export and post.
It’s reliable — and slow. If you need several clips a week, editing becomes the bottleneck.

sections.title: Upcut method
body: Paste the YouTube URL, pick duration and format, generate. Upcut suggests moments, renders vertical with subtitles, you download.
You keep control (manual mode = search window) without rebuilding a CapCut timeline every time.

sections.title: Checklist before posting
body: Hook visible on the first frame, text readable on mobile, no useless intro, light CTA at the end if you want to send people back to the long-form.

clips-twitch-automatiques.metaTitle: Automatic Twitch clips to TikTok & Reels | Upcut
clips-twitch-automatiques.metaDescription: Generate clips from a Twitch VOD: strong moments, vertical format, subtitles — workflow for streamers and clippers.
clips-twitch-automatiques.title: Automatic Twitch clips: from VOD to TikTok
clips-twitch-automatiques.lead: A 4-hour stream often holds 8–15 usable clips. The problem isn’t content — it’s cut time.

sections.title: Why Twitch clipping hurts
body: Scrub the VOD, find moments, reframe facecam / gameplay, subtitle, export… Multiply by clip count and the week is gone.
Clippers and small studios know: volume wins only if the process is industrializable.

sections.title: Recommended workflow
body: Use a published VOD (more stable than a live in progress). Set a target duration (e.g. 30–60s). Run moment detection, then filter: keep clips where energy / punchline is clear.
In manual mode, bound a zone (highlight, ranked, just chatting) so you don’t scan all 4 hours.

sections.title: Framing and split
body: Depending on content type (talk, gameplay, podcast), vertical reframing differs. Upcut uses adapted render modes — always check the preview before posting.

sections.title: Publishing cadence
body: Better 5 solid clips / week than a burst of 20 mediocre ones. Hook quality > raw quantity. Reuse best moments across TikTok, Reels, and Shorts with a slight title change.

pourquoi-shorts-ne-marchent-pas.metaTitle: Why my Shorts are not taking off | Upcut
pourquoi-shorts-ne-marchent-pas.metaDescription: Short diagnostic: hook, pacing, subtitles, topic, timing. Why your Shorts / Reels stall — and what to change.
pourquoi-shorts-ne-marchent-pas.title: Why my Shorts / Reels are not working
pourquoi-shorts-ne-marchent-pas.lead: Before blaming the algorithm, check the product. Most flatlining clips fail in the first five seconds.

sections.title: 1. No hook
body: If the first 3 seconds are an intro, a logo, or “hey guys”, you already lost. Start at the peak: punchline, fail, reveal.

sections.title: 2. Unreadable without sound
body: A huge share of the feed scrolls muted. Without clear subtitles (large, contrasted, synced), the clip dies.

sections.title: 3. Too long or too slow
body: A 90-second monologue with no cut or stakes fatigues. Cut silence, tighten. If the strong moment is 12 seconds, don’t stretch it to 45.

sections.title: 4. Wrong excerpt from long-form
body: Not everything is clippable. Look for tension, emotion, surprise, proof, light controversy — not the “context” chapter of your video.

sections.title: 5. Only then: distribution
body: Title / first line, native thumbnail (when available), post time, series. But if the clip is weak, distribution won’t save it.
Upcut helps you produce candidates faster — you keep the best and ruthlessly drop the rest.

sections.title: CapCut: control
body: Timeline, effects, templates, manual crop. Perfect for a signature clip. Less sustainable if you need 8 excerpts from a 3-hour VOD every week.

sections.title: Upcut: flow
body: Paste the URL, pick duration and format, get 9:16 MP4s with subtitles. You can still drop weak clips — you just don’t rebuild the timeline every time.

sections.title: When to keep CapCut
body: Heavy branding, motion design, one hero clip to polish. Many people do volume in Upcut, then finish 1 or 2 pieces in CapCut.

sections.title: Same problem
body: Too much long-form, not enough shorts. Both tools find moments and package vertical video with on-screen text.

sections.title: What Upcut owns
